<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/origin/pull/30914):

>## Summary
>
>- `IsMicroShiftCluster()` calls `skipper.Skip()` when the API poll times out, but when called from a Ginkgo **container node** context (e.g. `InitializeTestFramework` during suite setup), Ginkgo v2 panics — `Skip()` is only valid inside leaf nodes (`BeforeEach`, `It`, etc.)
>- When a prior recovery test leaves the cluster API returning 503, the 5-minute poll timeout triggers `Skip()` → panic → binary crash → all remaining tests cascade as failures
>- Replace `Skip()` with a log message and fall through returning `(false, nil)`. Framework init succeeds, and each test's own `BeforeEach` health checks (e.g. `SkipIfClusterIsNotHealthy`) properly skip the test
>
>### Impact
>
>Analysis of recent IPv6 TNF CI failures shows this cascade panic accounts for:
>- **11/12** IPv6 graceful re-addition failures
>- **12/12** IPv6 double-graceful failures
>
>These were previously misattributed to other bugs but are entirely caused by this `Skip()` panic.
>
>### Root cause
>
>```
>AddBeforeAll (container node)
>  → InitializeTestFramework()                    # binary.go:117
>    → IsMicroShiftCluster(coreClient)            # framework.go:2321
>      → wait.PollUntilContextTimeout(5m)         # polls API, gets 503s
>      → skipper.Skip(...)                        # framework.go:2345 — PANICS
>      → binary crash — "external binary did not produce a result"
>      → all remaining tests fail with (0s) 0001-01-01T00:00:00
>```
>
>### Fix
>
>```diff
> }); err != nil {
>-    // Timeout accessing the configmap is a precondition failure
>-    skipper.Skip(preconditions.FormatSkipMessage(fmt.Sprintf("microshift-version configmap check timed out after %s: %v", duration, err)))
>+    e2e.Logf("IsMicroShiftCluster: timed out after %s: %v (assuming not MicroShift)", duration, err)
> }
>```
>
>On timeout, log and assume not MicroShift. The function falls through to `cm == nil` → returns `(false, nil)`. Framework initialization succeeds. Each test's `BeforeEach` then runs `SkipIfClusterIsNotHealthy()`, which detects the unhealthy cluster and properly skips the test.
>
>## Test plan
>
>- [x] `go build ./test/extended/util/...` — compiles cleanly
>- [x] `go vet ./test/extended/util/...` — no warnings
>- [ ] CI: verify remaining tests are properly skipped (not crashed) when a recovery test leaves the API unavailable
>
